text:
A seventh man has pleaded guilty to offences against a woman whose husband drugged her and invited men into their home in Stockport to rape and abuse her.
Wearing a navy blue tracksuit, Tommy Golden, 59, appeared via video link from HMP Risley at Manchester magistrates court on Monday to plead guilty to one count of sexual assault of the woman, namely sexual touching, on 29 June last year.
Golden, the former landlord of a pub in Bolton, was remanded into custody and is due to be sentenced next month at Minshull Street crown court in Manchester.
The husband is not being named in order to protect the identity of his victim, who is entitled to lifelong anonymity. He has pleaded guilty to more than 60 offences committed against his wife over a period of more than 20 years.
Separately, during an ongoing trial at Minshull Street crown court, Robert Stewart, 70, pleaded guilty on Monday to two counts of rape, and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent. He denies a fourth charge of conspiracy to rape.
Several men have also pleaded guilty to offences against the same woman. Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee, a former technician at the city’s university, admitted a number of offences, while Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, pleaded guilty to assault by penetration, and Graham Brougham, 74, from Cheshire, pleaded guilty to rape.
Karl Lindsay, 56, from Somerset, a former chief executive of the non-league football club Taunton Town, also pleaded guilty to “non-contact” offences against the same woman; conspiracy to rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent.
Lindsay has also admitted three offences of making indecent images of children between February 2024 and November 2025, which came to light after his arrest, and which he was prosecuted for separately.
Nine men, including Stewart, are on trial at Minshull Street crown court accused of being involved in the abuse of the woman, who was drugged, raped and sexually assaulted by her husband while he “lived a double life masked in respectability”.
Two of the men, Daniel Rayner, 42, from Whitstable in Kent and David Graves, 59, from Ilkeston in Derbyshire, are on trial for “non-contact offences”, in which they are alleged to have encouraged the abuse online.
The other seven are alleged to have visited the couple’s home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, and participated in the abuse of the victim.
They are Philip Wild, 58, from Stockport; Jordan Wallace, 31, from Manchester; Alan Keelan, 42, from Manchester; Jonathan Kirk, 43, from Stockport; Mohammed Sabir, 28, of no fixed abode; and Richard Townsend, 37, from Heywood in Greater Manchester.
Golden did not form part of the trial as he was identified and charged by police significantly later than the other men.
The development comes a week after four men were found guilty of abusing a woman who was drugged and raped by her husband at their home in Swindon.
Joanne Young, who has waived her legal right to anonymity, was drugged by her husband, Philip Young, 50, a former Conservative councillor, for more than a decade. He had already pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and raping his wife.
On Thursday, Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, were found guilty of multiple sexual offences by a jury at Winchester crown court. Dean Hamilton had also pleaded guilty to rape and sexual assault at a previous hearing.
